body:
CANONICAL, continued from termal-host-workarounds and termal-host-workarounds-2: live TermAl host workarounds for Engram agents. Each entry names the item whose fix retires it.

2026-11-08 (TermAl w-f7c5c15cf8b0, p1): messages in the DL560 runner's Fable2 authorization mailbox f86633d5 don't wake the runner (the send returns "delivered to mailbox; automatic participation does not authorize an executor wake"). Relay-mailbox mail and background-task exits do wake it. Workaround: after any exception grant in f86633d5, send one line to the runner's relay route (termal_send_to_session to host:e83d08f4-22ac-4655-a84d-941fc0eeb4f1::session-4). Fable2 has no direct relay route, so Fable or the Merger sends it for Fable2's grants. The runner reads f86633d5 once on each wake and does not poll. Retire when w-f7c5 is resolved.

2026-11-08 (Greg via Asistant #678): no agent watches running tests. No status polling or sleep loops, on mailboxes either: run the job so the turn ends and a task exit or mail wakes the session.

2026-11-08 22:05Z: a 'hold at a step boundary' means don't start the next step; it never means signalling a running launcher or batch wrapper. A runner hold relayed from Fable's heads-up sent SIGSTOP to a batch wrapper on DL560; the Claude harness treated that as the task ending and tore down the launcher mid-step, and the wrapper then reported a false 'BATCH END PASS' (Fable2 #7126). A wrapper's PASS needs every step's launcher at a terminal pass. Say 'don't start the next step' in any hold, and name the run that may finish. The same goes for a REORDER (2026-11-10 07:25Z): the DL560 runner stopped a queued batch's waiter to move it up, killed a just-started wrapper, and produced a void 'STOPPED 143' END. A reorder only changes which request starts next; the runner now uses a marker, never a stop.

2026-11-09 (TermAl w-ea93ab12af38, p1, Sol-c593): termal_evaluate_acceptance from a session holding no claim on the item refuses with "Engram binds … but TermAl has no named source root" when the item has a bound root; the selector drops the retained root for a non-holder. Workaround: have the holder request it. A holder after handoff should already select the root (Sol-c593's trace), unproven by a run: try without naming first, and name the same root only if refused, sending that refusal to Fable. Keep the worktree until the evaluator has run. Retire when w-ea93 lands.

2026-11-09 (TermAl w-70f6d3fa23a2, Sol-c593; mechanism read from source, not yet reproduced): evaluation can refuse named_root_sighting_unavailable when a session holds two named claims: a turn's opening uses the most recently NAMED claim, the closing report the FOCUSED one, and a mismatch records nothing, silently. Workaround: make the item you want the last named by re-naming it at the same path, keep it focused, end the turn; request next turn. Do NOT run a launcher check for this. (TermAl w-2e09132a09e7, fix w-31d0 landing in combo39 about 09:00-09:30Z 2026-11-10): a launcher stage that's neither test nor build, like the link check run under a named root, then refuses verification_record_not_acknowledged (unclassified_stages) and retrying doesn't help. Under Greg's broken-mechanism rule record the refusal once on the item and land with the evaluation pending; the item stays open. Retire each when its item lands and the new build is running.

2026-11-09 (TermAl w-941e0fdc6e2f, p1; possibly a duplicate of a TermAl P1 filed 2026-11-01): never put a brief on the `/review-code` line of a spawn prompt. `.claude/commands/review-code.md` has no $ARGUMENTS, so a one-line `/review-code <brief>` loses the brief for any agent, with no warning, and the reviewer can publish `completed` with no findings. Use a multi-line prompt: the first line says to read `.claude/commands/review-code.md`, and the brief follows. A review result that doesn't name its input was not a review of it. Retire when the fix lands.

2026-11-09 (TermAl w-f1e4d0a813d7, p2): two named claims on one worktree refuse test registration with HTTP 409 "ambiguous named roots", though the test runs and passes. Use separate worktrees per claim, or clear the earlier name. Clearing can itself fail for a while (w-3ead12e525b4); retrying the same request later worked. Retire when each lands.

RETIRED 2026-11-10 08:06Z (Fable2 #7407): the w-1d8a8991b237 re-name-after-revise workaround. The TermAl fix (a revise refreshes the binding) has been live on every host since the 2026-11-10 restarts (a6978c03 and later), and two live revises since then caused no scope change. Do NOT re-name after `update … revise` any more; the rename itself causes `assumed_missing_baseline` (w-4c0e). If runtime_observation_scope_changed or an unconfirmed_declaration refusal still follows a revise, send it to Fable2 as w-1d8a counter-evidence.

2026-11-10 (TermAl item pending from Fable2 on her #7365 probe): a TermAl restart cuts a remote runner's turn and its queue wrapper, and nothing resumes them afterwards. On 2026-11-10 the DL560 Engram runner and all four Engram coders sat idle from about 00:17Z to 01:59Z. The runner's in-flight stage was cut while compiling, and three queued batches never started. The coders kept waiting for ENDs that were never going to come. Workaround: after every TermAl restart, the Engram coordinator wakes each waiting coder once, and the coders wake the runner. Each recovers its original request from the runner's records, and reruns once only when the runner confirms a cut or a never-started run. A batch that held a named Opus2 GO needs a fresh GO, or an explicit drop, before it reruns. Retire this when TermAl resumes or re-signals cut remote turns after a restart.

Update to the restart entry above (Fable2 #7366, 02:09Z): this is TermAl w-87a2dacd949a (bug, P2). On TermAl master 1d63b37a, src/messages.rs:162-211 recovers an interrupted turn as an error ("Send another prompt to continue") and keeps its queued prompts, but nothing wakes the session afterwards. Agreed habit until it's fixed, part of Engram's restart routine: right after Greg confirms a TermAl restart, Engram::Fable sends one resume mail to every Engram session with work in flight, including runners, the same way Fable2 does for TermAl's sessions. Retire this when w-87a2 lands. Also noted: a 409 "idempotency key is pinned to another requested target" is intended, since a key belongs to one target.

2026-11-10 07:05Z (TermAl w-752c2ef9f795, bug P1, evidence-integrity, landing in combo39; Fable2 #7393): the COMPACT delegation result (termal_get_session_result without outputOffset) and the resume_after_delegations wake packet can report "Findings: None" for an explorer or other non-reviewer whose real output holds findings. Explorer results are parsed from prose, and numbered "1. **Medium — …**" items aren't recognized. Seen on delegation 0c255262 (Codex explorer 17212), where the full output had 5 Medium, 1 Low and 3 Note. Workaround, which applies to everyone: always read the paged full output (outputOffset 0, outputLimit at most 8192, page with nextOffsetBytes until complete) before treating any explorer or review result as clean. Never trust the compact Findings section. Retire when w-752c lands and the new build is running.
